title: The Armchair Salvage Club
teaser: The treasure is coming to you. You will not need to stand up.
clue: Something precious is out at sea, and the tide only comes in as fast as you let it.
reveal: A cloth raft carries treasure slowly across the floor to your seated dog, who may greet it, sniff it and open it at their own pace.
objective: Bring a small treasure to your dog's bed on a slow floor-level raft, with no jumping or walking required.
instructions: Settle your dog on a bed or rug on a non-slip floor, a few steps from your chair. You stay seated; the club meets in comfort.

Make the raft: a smooth dish towel or sheet on a bare floor. Give it a name and a paper flag to wave as it sets sail. Place the treasure on it: a favorite soft toy, with a few pieces of usual food in a fold of cloth if your dog enjoys that.
From a few meters away, pull the corner of the raft slowly toward you, like a tide coming in. Never pull it away from your dog, and stop the second they show interest.
Let your dog watch, sniff, walk over or just wait. Take the flag off, let the raft dock at their bed or paws, and nobody has to get up.
Once it docks, your dog may open the treasure, sniff it, lick the cloth or ignore it. Whatever they choose counts.
For round two, load a new treasure: a cloth that smells of a favorite place, or a different toy, and sail again.
twist: The adventure travels to your dog: a cloth raft carries the treasure slowly across the floor so your dog can claim it without standing up, jumping or hurrying.
variations: Carpet: use a smooth bath mat as the raft.
No food: use toys and scent cloths only.
Very short voyage: start only a meter away.
Two dogs: sail one raft at a time, with a cloth each.
completion: A treasure has docked and your dog has met it in whatever way they like.
photoIdea: The raft docked at the bed, with the treasure and your dog's nose near it.
memoryPrompt: How did your dog greet the raft, and which treasure was the favorite?
supplies: A paper flag (kept out of reach)
optionalSupplies: A few pieces of usual food
A cloth that smells of a favorite place
substitutes: No dish towel? A smooth pillowcase.
No soft toy? Any large soft toy too big to swallow.
dietNotes: Use only a few pieces of the usual diet, or skip food. Ask your vet about your senior dog's diet.
safety: Keep the pulling slow and never drag it away; stop if your dog tenses or grabs and pulls.
Keep it on a non-slip floor with no jumping, stairs or sharp turns; take away anything chewed apart.
Follow your vet's advice on activity, and stop when your dog has had enough.

keepsake.headline: SALVAGE CLUB MEMBER
keepsake.explainer: The treasure came to me. I did not even stand up
